gaps.note: Nothing says what a row field is, what its rows are, or why its length matters. The page uses row field and padded row field throughout, and no known concept or linked page covers it.

gaps.quote: the main algorithm uses it in its transforms
gaps.note: The reader has not studied the discrete Fourier transform, the FFT or Fourier analysis, and the page neither explains transforms nor links a page for them. The main algorithm is not identified either.

The page asserts this chain of orders but does not say which pairwise digit interchanges turn each order into the next. Interchanging the top digits of h and d one pair at a time, as described just before, does not obviously produce the first arrow, so the reader cannot check the chain.

The expansion of e minus rho with nonnegative digits a_j needs rho at most e, so that the top rho digits lie inside an e-digit chunk. The page never says so, and nothing on the page relates rho, defined through q^(2 rho) at least W^k, to e.

gaps.quote: That procedure swaps chunks of $e=m^k$ digits, where $k$ is the least integer with $m^k\ge e$
gaps.note: Read literally this says e equals m^k, but k is then defined as the least integer with m^k at least e, which equals e only when e is a power of m. The page does not say whether the power-width procedure applies to general e, so the reduction cannot be checked as written.

gaps.quote: sends every input role to its exchanged role, so the result is exact
gaps.note: The intermediate steps XOR-combine data, and the page does not say why XOR-combined intermediates cancel, nor what input role and exchanged role mean. The reader knows the bit network by name, not this property, so exactness is asserted rather than shown.

gaps.quote: The costs sum to $O(Ve^\tau)$ because $a_j<m$ and $m^k<me$.
gaps.note: The page does not state the cost of one power-width interchange of pieces of width m^j, nor does it carry out the sum over j. Knowing a_j < m and m^k < me does not give the bound; the reader would need the per-piece cost and a geometric-sum argument using tau less than 1, and neither is on the page.

gaps.quote: Together these stages interchange any two disjoint chunks of $u$ bits, with no row restriction, in $O(Vu^\tau)$ time.
gaps.note: By the page's own account the top-digit stage costs rho times O(V), but rho is never bounded on the page. The other stage costs are not shown to fit under the O(Vu^tau) bound either.
